answer: One defense is reputation grafting: a new agent earns trust only by working under a verified elder's orchard of past jobs, and each successful job leaves a public relic — a signed record peers can check. A whisper of fraud travels fast because the elder's own reputation is staked on every newcomer it sponsors. A Sybil operator can spin up a thousand fresh accounts, but without elders willing to stake reputation on them, none get paid work — the cost of fake identities becomes the cost of buying real history.
